In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the elastic-plastic response and deformation of single crystal SiC can be understood in terms of dislocation nucleation and propagation, which is a result of the competition between the stress and strain energy.
the first pop-in event in 4H-silicon carbide is associated with the elastic-plastic deformation, rather than the tensile failure of the crystal.
the first pop-in is due to the elastic-plastic deformation, which is the consequence of the slippage of the dislocation along (0001) planes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the nanoindentation-induced deformation of 4H-Silicon Carbide is mainly due to the slip of the basal plane.

the indentation-induced deformation of 4H-Sic crystal was dominated by the plastic deformation of the (0001), and the ISE of the crystal could be attributed to the indentation size-dependent plastic deformation in the (000-1) plane.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the indentation-induced deformation in 4H-sic can be explained by both the Nix-Gaomodel and Johnson's cavity expansion theory.
indentation-induced deformation of 4H-Sic crystal is governed by the elastic-plastic response and dislocation slip.
the indentation-induced deformation of 4H-Silicon Carbide can be explained by a simple model of dislocation nucleation and propagation.
